lifecycle.title: Service lifecycle
lifecycle.warning: Restarting or stopping the service can be irreversible without administrator intervention. The dashboard may disconnect immediately after confirmation.

restart.title: Restart service?
restart.description: The service will record the request in audit, drain current connections, and start again with the same arguments.

stop.title: Stop service?
stop.description: The service will shut down and may remain offline until an administrator starts it again.

accountMode.title: Account mode
accountMode.onlyAccount: Officer acts on the account {{account}} only.
accountMode.createsAccount: No account exists yet: Officer creates the account {{account}} and acts on it only.

otherAccounts.title: The other accounts stop working
otherAccounts.detail: They stay in the database and work again once the mode is switched back to several accounts.

confirm.title: Save the account mode?
confirm.description: If the running mode changes, Officer restarts to apply it: the panel disconnects and reloads when Officer is back.

accountMode.saved: The account mode is saved. No restart is needed.
accountMode.restarting: Officer is restarting; the panel reloads when it is back.

restartNotice.title: Restart needed to apply the account mode
restartNotice.detail: The saved account mode differs from the mode the running service enforces. Restart the service to apply it.

database.title: Database
database.resetDescription: Delete every row, recreate the database from scratch, and rebuild the engine. Export a backup first if you may need the current data.
database.resetConfirm: Delete all data and recreate the database from scratch? Export a backup first if you may need the current data.

plaintextKeys.title: This backup will contain keys in plain text
plaintextKeys.trading: API keys of trading connections go into the archive unencrypted.
plaintextKeys.marketData: API keys and tokens of market-data sources go into the archive unencrypted.
plaintextKeys.advice: Keep the file private, or set a master key first.

backup.tradingSectionsHint: Trading connections include accounts and groups, and orders and trades; orders and trades include trading connections.
backup.tradingAccountsHint: Trading data is exported and restored for all accounts.
backup.tradingCredentialsUnavailable: API keys could not be restored for <connections/>. Those trading connections were restored disabled: enter their keys again in <tradingLink>Trading connections</tradingLink>.
backup.title: Database backup
backup.marketDataCredentialsUnavailable: Credentials could not be opened for {{instances}}. Those market-data sources were restored disabled and need their credentials entered again.
backup.confirmReplaceAll: Delete all selected data and restore this backup?
backup.restoreScopeWarning: Restore modes apply to the data selected above, not to the entire database unless All data is checked.

access.boundary: An agent, a script or a person with a terminal on this computer under your user controls Officer fully, past the token and the password: with Docker Desktop through <exec/>, a copy of the data volume and <inspect/>; without Docker through Officer's data folder. The token and the password keep out web pages, other containers, and agents in a sandbox that cannot reach Docker or Officer's files.

isolation.title: Run an agent that cannot touch Officer
isolation.sandbox: In a sandbox without the Docker socket and without access to Officer's data.
isolation.user: Under a separate user account on this computer.

token.title: Token and password
token.description: Programs and agents show a token. The panel asks for a password once per browser.

open.title: No token
open.description: Any software on this computer uses Officer without being asked.

password.hint: At least {{min}} characters. Keep it in your password manager.

facts.session: The panel asks for it once per browser and keeps you logged in for up to 30 days. A week without visits, or logging out, ends the session.
facts.agent: Your agent gets its own token. It works only over MCP, within the commands you allow.
facts.programs: Your own programs get an API token on Service › Security.
facts.recovery: Forgot the password? Officer prints a one-time recovery code to its log.

warning.title: Without a token, Officer is open to everything on this computer
warning.containers: any container on Docker's default network;
warning.agents: any AI agent with a terminal here - it calls the REST API directly and steps around the limits you set for it in MCP.
warning.what: What they can do: read everything, change and remove limits, unblock accounts, turn on agent commands, delete all data, send orders through your trading connections.
warning.pages: Web pages open in your browser stay locked out in both modes.
warning.close: To close it, choose Token and password and set a panel password. Officer switches at once, without a restart.
warning.acknowledge: I understand: any software on this computer can control Officer.

masterKeyGuide.where: Do this in a terminal on this computer
masterKeyGuide.chooseSystem: Choose the system of this computer to see its commands.

create.title: Create the key file
create.detail: 32 random bytes, in a folder only you can open.
create.detailDocker: 32 random bytes, in a folder only you can open. The file itself stays readable, so Officer's container can read it.

keep.title: Keep a copy of the key somewhere else
keep.detail: Put it into your password manager, or print it and store it safely. Lose the key and Officer never opens its database again: there is no recovery.

start.title: Start Officer again with the key
start.detailDocker: This replaces the container. Your data stays in the volume <volume/>.
start.detailBinary: Stop the running <running/> with <keys/>, then start it like this, with the options you used before.

access.title: Access

switchDialog.title: Switch to no token?
switchDialog.description: Officer deletes the panel password, both tokens and every browser session, then answers any program on this computer without a token.

changeDialog.title: Change the panel password
changeDialog.description: Every other browser is logged out; this one stays logged in.

access.passwordChanged: The panel password is changed. Every other browser is logged out.

agent.label: Agent token · MCP
agent.note: The same token as in Connect your agent on MCP access. Regenerating stops the old one at once.
agent.confirmDescription: The current agent token stops working at once: an agent that uses it loses MCP until its configuration gets the new one.

api.label: API token · REST
api.note: Full control over REST - the same access the panel holds through its session. Never give it to an agent.
api.confirmDescription: The current API token stops working at once: a program that uses it loses REST until it gets the new one.

storage.title: Storage, signing and accounts
storage.plainText: Off · stored keys are plain text

exposed.title: Secrets stored before the master key was set must be considered exposed
exposed.detail_one: Sealing re-encrypted {{count}} stored secret that had lain in the database file as plain text: anyone who copied the file or a backup before then can read it.
exposed.detail_other: Sealing re-encrypted {{count}} stored secrets that had lain in the database file as plain text: anyone who copied the file or a backup before then can read them.
exposed.keys: Issue new keys with your providers and enter them on the connection pages.
exposed.signing: If a signing key was stored, generate a new one: whoever holds a copy of the old key can sign decisions in Officer's name.
exposed.tokens: Regenerate both tokens: each old value stops working at once.

guide.label: First-run guide
guide.value: Every step, with your current choices
